The factual matrix of the prosecution case are as under:
The marriage of deceased-Smt. Geetha was solemnized with the accused No.1 on 22.05.2009 and at the time of marriage on demand he received gold ring, gold chain,
gold bracelet, wrist watch, cloths etc., as dowry from the parents of deceased-Smt.
Geetha.

After the marriage deceased-Smt. Geetha started residing with family members of accused No.1 in a rented house situated Yusuf Building, Ramesh Nagara,
within the limits of HAL P.S., Bangalore.

The accused No.1 and 2, subjected her to physical and mental cruelty by demanding additional dowry in terms of Rs.3,00,000/- by abusing and assaulting and threatened to oust her, and by putting fear on her, accused No.1 took the deceased and left her in the house of her parents,
and by feeling hurt the deceased residing at her parents house.

On 6.10.2009 deceased over phone requested the accused No.1 to take back her to matrimonial house, the accused No.1 by abusing refused to take back her without additional dowry, by feeling hurt and disgusting the deceased- Smt. Geetha consumed acid,
which was brought for cleaning the bathroom, and become unconscious, the parents of complainant have admitted her to hospital.

In that regard the deceased made a statement before Rajagopalanagar P.S., based on the statement of deceased-Smt.
Geetha the Rajagopalanagar Police have registered FIR in Crime No.411/2009 for the offences punishable U/s.498A and 506 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of DP Act and on the point of jurisdiction, the case has been transferred to the complainant police, and complainant police have registered the crime No.515/2009 in their police Station and 12.03.2010 the deceased succumbed to the burn injuries due to acid consumption.

Accordingly, the case was registered against the accused persons for subjecting the deceased for mental and physical cruelty and abetting the deceased to commit suicide in demand of additional dowry within seven years from the date of marriage.

If Sec.304B of IPC is r/w Sec.113B of Evidence Act, a comprehensive picture emerges that if a married women dies in an unnatural circumstances at her matrimonial home within seven years from her marriage and there are allegations of cruelty or harassment upon such married women for or in connection with demand of dowry by the husband or relatives of the husband, the case would squarely come under dowry death and there shall be presumption against the husband and the relatives.

In order to hold an accused guilt of an offence U/s.304B of IPC it has to be shown that apart from the fact that the women died on account of burn or bodily injury, otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, it has also to be shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with any demand for dowry.

Only then would such death be called dowry death and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused death of women concerned as held in 2010 AIR SCW 3673(Durgaprasad and another Vs., State of AP) .

sentences.text: Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in 2020(5) KCCR 905 (Mahalingappla Vs., State of Karnataka) held that death of victim within seven years from the date of marriage alone can not be ground to convict the accused.

In the case on hand also the deceased-Smt. Geetha was admittedly dropped by accused No.1 to her parents house,
even two months before her unnatural death.
Alleged telephone conversation between accused No.1 and deceased soon before her death is not established by the prosecution by leading acceptable evidence to prove the demand of dowry.
Accordingly, the prosecution failed to prove the charge leveled against accused No.1 and 2 and hence, I answered points No.1 to 4 in the Negative.
23. Point No.3:

In view of answer of points No.1 to 4, this I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 and 2 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A and 304B r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of DP Act.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The accused No.1 and 2, subjected her to physical and mental cruelty by demanding additional dowry in terms of Rs.3,00,000/- by abusing and assaulting and threatened to oust her, and by putting fear on her, accused No.1 took the deceased and left her in the house of her parents, and by feeling hurt the deceased residing at her parents house.
Because of consumption of acid, her internal organs damaged she was able to consume liquid food and the medical officer, who examined her in Sarvodaya Hospital, after going through the scanning report, advised her parents to discharge the deceased and she was shifted to her parents house, where she breathed last on 12.03.2010.
Based on oral evidence of the relatives of the deceased as well as her statement it cannot be said that demand for additional dowry is established by the prosecution.
The physical and mental cruelty to the deceased soon before her death and payment of dowry by way of ornaments to the accused persons, as well as demand for additional dowry of Rs.3,00,000/- and dowry death has not been established with avaialbe evidence on record.
The basic ingredients to attract the provisions of Sec.304B are (I) the death of the women should be caused by burns or fatal injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances;
(ii) Such death should have occurred within seven years of her marriage (iii) she must have been subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband;
(iv)such cruelty and harassment should be for in connection with demand for dowry.

Only then would such death be called dowry death and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused death of women concerned as held in 2010 AIR SCW 3673(Durgaprasad and another Vs., State of AP) .
